newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Mahathir shies away from corruption specifics.
newsitem.headline: Mahathir shies away from corruption specifics.

text.p: Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said on Friday that there are indications of "money politics" by Malaysia corporations, but shied away from specific charges.

Asked if major corporations in Malaysia are participating in vote buying and other irregularities commonly referred to as money politics in Malaysia, Mahathir said: "There are indications, of course, but I do not like to presume anything until I have the correct information."
"It is not fair to make accusations when you are not certain," he said.
On Thursday, a tearful Mahathir warned delegates at the United Malays National Organisation (UMNO) election assembly that greed and money politics would destroy the 50-year-old party.

The prime minister, who is also UMNO president, has made the corruption issue a battle cry of this four-day convention. He even ordered a blanket ban on campaigning for the 66 offices up for grabs to keep candidates from showering money and favours on delegates.
Mahathir also sidestepped questions about whether candidates who lost their positions in the elections were being viewed as guilty of money politics.
"Only the delegates will know," he said. "I told the delegates, 'Reject those who try to bribe you.' They may reject for that, or they may reject for other reasons."
Among those unseated in this week's elections was incumbent International Trade and Industry Minister Rafidah Aziz, who narrowly lost the leadership of the women's wing of the party.
Two other top UMNO officials, youth leader Rahim Tamby Chik and Sports Minister Muhyiddin Yassin were also knocked out of their party positions.
